source.title: Toward Moderate Overparameterization: Global Convergence Guarantees for Training Shallow Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports theoretical convergence guarantees and numerical experiments on random labels for shallow networks, bearing on the ability to fit them. Its models and settings differ from the original deep image-classification experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper’s discussion of prior label-shuffling experiments is cited prior work, not a result from this study. It reports no test error or results on true labels.
record.test_reason: The study tests the random-label fitting component of V1 through convergence guarantees and synthetic experiments on shallow regression networks. It does not reproduce the original deep classification experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish conditional global convergence for sufficiently overparameterized shallow networks and report synthetic experiments suggesting fitting can succeed when kd only slightly exceeds n. They distinguish this empirical threshold from their stronger theoretical requirements and leave generalization unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies one-hidden-layer networks with fixed output weights and trains input-to-hidden weights, using Gaussian random inputs and labels in its experiments. It does not reproduce the original deep image-classification setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported fitting boundary varies with input dimension, hidden width, activation, and dataset size; the text says random-data phase transitions may differ for worst-case datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 3.2 establishes perfect interpolation by fitting output weights over fixed random hidden features when the feature matrix has full row rank.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide random-feature networks can interpolate arbitrary scalar targets through output-layer least squares.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory
record.problems: The numerical experiments use only 10 realizations per (k, d) pair and synthetic random inputs and Gaussian regression labels. Results are shown as heatmaps without extracted numeric probabilities. The paper explicitly notes that worst-case datasets may exhibit different phase transitions. It does not evaluate test error or true-label generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out. The paper’s cited label-shuffling experiments are prior work and excluded.

untested.parts: Standard deep classification architectures, chance-level test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters between true-label and random-label training. Experiments use shallow scalar regression with Gaussian targets and fixed output weights.
Random-versus-true-label training-time ratio and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs with the same networks. The numerical inputs are uniform on the unit sphere.
A corruption-fraction sweep with simultaneous perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise; no clean/noisy learning trajectories are compared.

missing.what: Theorem 2.5 gives an additional arbitrary-target fitting guarantee for ReLU networks under pairwise input separation, requiring k ≥ C(1+ν)²n⁹∥X∥⁶/δ⁴.
Split R1–R4 into successful, transitional, and unsuccessful parameter settings where figure values are available; the current aggregate rows cannot identify each condition's fitting probability.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical results concern arbitrary scalar targets, which include random targets. Their sufficient parameter-count bounds do not establish that fitting fails below those bounds. Missing deep-network and test-error measurements are untested components, not evidence against V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test deep image-classification networks, test error at chance, or whether the same networks generalize well on true labels. The numerical experiment uses one-hidden-layer regression networks and Gaussian random inputs and labels.
The paper gives convergence bounds and iteration counts but does not compare training time for random versus true labels or sweep the fraction of corrupted labels.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
No sweep from clean labels to fully random labels or paired training and test error results.
No comparison of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation, nor removal of those methods.
No measurement of learning order or comparison of real and random labels over training.

rows.note: The guarantee concerns expected squared residual on an event; the paper states that SGD converges to a global optimum close to initialization.
rows.check: The event probability is recorded incorrectly: the bound is 1−ν⁻⁴[3B∥X∥/(μ_phi σ_min(X*X))]/(kd), rather than using √(kd). Equation 2.10 bounds E[∥f(W_tau)−y∥² 1_E], not an unconditional expected residual.

source_check.correct: Equation (2.10) bounds E[||f(W_tau)−y||₂² 1_E] by a geometric factor times ||f(W_0)−y||₂². The initialization probability is at least 1−1/n−exp(−δ²n/(2||X||²)). Event E concerns SGD randomness conditional on initialization.
source_check.problem: The residual bound is verified, but the flattened event-probability formula does not reliably place its powers and fractions; the pack's proposed division-by-kd correction cannot be confirmed.
